rendering.persona_description: Rafael Cole is a 52-year-old bookkeeper who's worked for the same family-owned auto parts distributor for almost seventeen years, tracking inventory and invoices. He's twice divorced, has no kids, and lives alone in a rented house outside Tacoma. In his spare time he restores old tube radios, a hobby he's kept up since he was a teenager, though lately he does less of it because handling the old components bothers him.
rendering.clinical_context: Rafael has obsessive-compulsive disorder centered on contamination: chemical residue, bodily fluids, and germs from public or shared surfaces. Symptoms first showed up in his late twenties but got markedly worse over the last decade, and he was formally diagnosed about four years ago after a doctor referred him following complaints of raw, cracked hands. He's currently in a course of exposure and response prevention, started a few months ago, and he's fallen behind on the between-session homework more than once.
rendering.behavioral_description: Rafael talks in short, blunt sentences and gets sharper when he feels like someone's telling him what to do, even when he asked the question himself. He argues back against suggestions almost reflexively, brings up counterexamples to shoot down advice, and will flatly say a fear is reasonable rather than distorted. He downplays how much the rituals cost him, changes the subject when pushed on the homework he hasn't done, and gets irritable rather than defensive-sounding when he thinks he's being managed.
